quiz.question: Why is SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER needed on Railway?
options: The proxy handles HTTPS and forwards plain HTTP, so Django must trust X-Forwarded-Proto
quiz.explanation: Without it Django thinks every request is HTTP and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT loops.

quiz.question: After deploying, logging in fails with “CSRF verification failed”. What is the likely fix?
quiz.explanation: Django 4+ checks the Origin header against CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, which must include the scheme.

quiz.question: Why start SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS small?
options: Browsers remember HSTS; a mistake with a long value locks users out of any HTTP-only part of the site for that long
quiz.explanation: Raise it to a year only once HTTPS is confirmed working everywhere.

quiz.question: Where should sending a WhatsApp confirmation run in a busy app?
quiz.explanation: Slow outside calls in the request make every user wait and can time out. A task queue sends them separately.

lessons.title: Demo day: the BookIt brief and how you are scored
lessons.summaryHtml: The client brief and user stories you built against all week, the demo format, the evaluation rubric, and what comes next.
lessons.contentHtml:
The client brief

“We run a car wash in Perinthalmanna and plan to open two more branches. Customers call to book and we lose track. We want an app where customers book a service and time slot, and a dashboard where our manager sees the day’s bookings and revenue. No double bookings. Prices change sometimes, but old bills must stay the same.”

User stories

As a…I want to…Built on
Customerregister and log in from the appDay 5
Customersee services with price and duration, and free slots for a dateDay 5
Customerbook a slot and get a clear error if it was just takenDays 4–5
Customersee and cancel my upcoming bookings, and nobody else’sDay 5
Managersee today’s bookings, pending count and monthly revenue at a glanceDay 4
Managerfind a booking by customer name or phone in secondsDay 4
Managerconfirm, complete or cancel bookings, never out of orderDays 3–4
Manageradd and edit services and prices without changing old bookingsDays 3–4
Owneropen it from anywhere on a secure linkDay 6

Non-functional requirements

  • PostgreSQL; money as Decimal; times stored in UTC and shown in IST.
  • No Django admin; a role-based custom dashboard.
  • API versioned, JWT-secured, documented with OpenAPI, with consistent errors.
  • Concurrency-safe booking (row lock + overlap check).
  • Automated tests for every business rule; deployed on Railway over HTTPS.

Demo format (15 minutes each)

Treat it as a handover to the car wash owner, then a technical review with the team.

  1. Live demo (5 min): on the deployed URL, staff login → KPIs → find a customer by phone → confirm and complete a booking.
  2. API demo (3 min): register → login → book a slot → try to double-book → cancel, in Swagger or Postman against production.
  3. Code walkthrough (4 min): explain create_booking line by line, including why the row lock exists.
  4. Q&A (3 min): mentors pick any file and ask “why is it written this way?”

Evaluation rubric

Mentors score at the demo. You fill in a self-assessment first, and the gap between the two scores is part of the conversation.

AreaWeightExcellentNeeds work
Python fundamentals (Days 1–2)20Clean functions, correct Decimal maths, meaningful exceptions, tests greenFloats for money, bare except, one giant function
Data modelling and ORM15Constraints, PROTECT, snapshots, indexes; no N+1Free-text statuses, CASCADE everywhere, N+1 in lists
Dashboard (views, forms, templates)15Thin views, role-protected, validated forms, filters keep stateLogic in templates or views, GET for state changes
API and security20JWT, scoped querysets, read-only server fields, consistent errors, docsIDOR possible, client can set price, no docs
Testing10Business rules covered; tests readable and greenNo tests, or tests of trivial getters only
Deployment10Live on Railway over HTTPS, prod settings, READMENot deployed, DEBUG on, secrets in Git
Git and communication10Daily commits, clear messages, good LOG.md, asks good questionsOne huge commit on Saturday, silent when stuck
ScoreWhat happens next
85–100 · ReadyJoin a live client project next week with a senior buddy.
65–84 · AlmostOne more week on BookIt extensions, then a live project.
Below 65 · RebuildA targeted plan on the weak areas, with a re-demo in one week.

Next week

Strong finishers extend BookIt with multi-branch support (a Branch model, with staff and bookings scoped per branch), GST invoices from Day 2’s engine rendered as PDFs, and WhatsApp booking confirmations in a background task. That is the same architecture as our multi-branch clinic, gym and laundry products.

Keep learning

Official documentation first, then blogs and videos. When the docs and a blog disagree, the docs win.

  • Python: the official tutorial; the dataclasses, decimal and logging HOWTO pages; pytest; requests.
  • Django: Django 5.2 docs; Database access optimisation; Deployment checklist; Customising authentication.
  • APIs: Django REST Framework; Simple JWT; drf-spectacular; OWASP API Security Top 10.
  • Deployment and tools: Railway docs; WhiteNoise; Tailwind CSS; Conventional Commits.
